title: Hackathon Day
objective: Build and test a Catan agent that wins consistently.
current_focus: OneVOne won 609/1,000 fresh official-harness games against F with no faults or CPU overruns. Earlier win/loss and component audits point to early economy and expansion as the next candidate areas; V2 changes remain unimplemented.

entries.title: Official kit logistics and requirements
entries.objective: Establish the official interface, compute budget, evaluation and submission process.
entries.setup: Inspected lyric-hyde/catan-hackathon-agent at commit 04fffac90e00610f60e0b06d919f262f4b3ed9db: README, problem statement, requirements and harness source.
entries.result: Created LOGISTICS.md. No agent training or game evaluation was run.
entries.learning: The official harness enforces a 1.5-second maximum CPU allowance per game; eligibility and runtime rules must guide new work.
entries.next_step: Pass the official self-check, implement the event agent interface and run a 20-game smoke test.

entries.title: Self-contained OneVOne adapter and official environment
entries.objective: Port the existing heuristic to the official observation/index interface without changing its coefficients.
entries.setup: Pinned official kit 04fffac and engine d3f4ad0; separate Python 3.11.15 environment; copied four helper/policy modules plus configuration and a new entry point.
entries.result: Official self-check passed, including reference seed, deterministic replay and example-agent CPU checks. All scoring weights and tactical search limits preserved.
entries.learning: The old workspace engine was a different commit; isolated official-engine evaluation is necessary. The heuristic needs no ML packages, so unused ML-wheel downloads were stopped and omitted.
entries.next_step: Measure wins, faults and CPU under the official clock. Preserve provenance before considering submission eligibility.

entries.title: OneVOne official-harness smoke test
entries.objective: Check the adapter plays legally and fits the official CPU clock.
entries.setup: 20 games / 10 boards, both seats; seeds 2026101700–2026101709; official examples/f_agent.py; clock enforced.
entries.result: 13/20 wins (65%); 97.2 ms mean / 246.2 ms worst CPU per game; 0 errors in 870 decisions, 0 overruns, 0 timeouts/crashes.
entries.learning: Interface and timing passed this smoke test. Twenty games are too few for a stable strength estimate.
entries.next_step: Run 200 games on 100 different paired boards against F.

entries.title: OneVOne initial baseline against official F
entries.objective: Establish a measured starting win rate under the official harness.
entries.setup: 200 games / 100 boards, both seats; seeds 2026101800–2026101899; official examples/f_agent.py; original coefficients and tactical limits.
entries.result: 127/200 wins (63.5%); reported 95% interval ±6.67 percentage points; 111.4 ms mean / 333.3 ms worst CPU per game; 0 errors in 9,934 decisions; 0 clock overruns, timeouts or crashes.
entries.learning: The copied policy runs successfully against official F and exceeded 50% wins on this initial screen. This establishes a starting baseline, not an improvement over another candidate or a result against O. CPU was measured on local macOS, not the organizer machine.
entries.next_step: Freeze this baseline, record detailed losing-game decisions, and compare one controlled change at a time on paired boards. Verify CPU on the organizer machine.

entries.title: Replay and diagnosis of all 200 baseline games
entries.objective: Compare how wins and losses develop under the official rules.
entries.setup: Engine-side observation of the same 100 boards in both seats; frozen agent hashes verified; official observation boundary and clocks preserved.
entries.result: Reproduced 127 wins, 73 losses and 9,934 decisions with zero faults or overruns. First additional settlement: mean turn 25.9 in wins versus 32.8 in losses, among games where built. In 58/73 losses we finished at seven VP or below.
entries.learning: An economy and expansion gap is visible by turn 20. These outcome-grouped differences are associations, not proof that a particular heuristic caused the losses.
entries.next_step: Use the recorded losing positions to isolate resource and expansion decisions; compare controlled changes on fresh boards.

entries.title: Four controlled component removals
entries.objective: Measure which existing OneVOne components contribute against official F.
entries.setup: Four isolated copies, 200 games each on the baseline board/seat schedule; 800 diagnostic games total; no baseline edits.
entries.result: Tactical override disabled: 118/200 (59.0%); default value weights: 122/200 (61.0%); generic robber: 127/200 (63.5%); late development bonus removed: 122/200 (61.0%). All runs had zero faults and overruns.
entries.learning: The tactical layer has the strongest positive signal in this screen. All paired 95% intervals for differences include or touch zero; fresh confirmation is needed. Effects cannot be added together.
entries.next_step: Preserve the baseline and test proposed V2 changes independently; confirm any gains on fresh paired boards.

entries.title: Guaranteed-win and Monopoly decision audit
entries.objective: Find concrete decision mistakes without changing the playing agent.
entries.setup: 1,199 saved masked positions; bounded deterministic search at 294 selected late-game positions, depth up to three actions; exact-resource scoring of 33 selected Monopoly plays.
entries.result: Found 13 positions across 11 games with guaranteed winning alternatives: ten development purchases and three end-turn decisions. Five Monopoly plays took zero cards; nine chose a resource with a lower exact successor score. All of these findings were in games eventually won.
entries.learning: The development-card shortcut, two-action search depth and production-based Monopoly estimate have reproducible limitations. These findings do not explain the 73 losses and do not establish a win-rate gain from fixing them.
entries.next_step: Test exact visible resource transfers and guaranteed-win handling separately, then investigate the broader early-game deficit.

entries.title: OneVOne fresh 1,000-game run against official F
entries.objective: Estimate the frozen heuristic's win rate against the supplied F bot on more unseen boards.
entries.setup: 1,000 games / 500 boards, both seats; seeds 2026200000–2026200499; official examples/f_agent.py; original coefficients and tactical limits; official local clock enforced.
entries.result: 609/1,000 wins (60.9%); evaluator 95% interval ±3.02 percentage points; 118.8 ms mean / 494.3 ms worst CPU per game; 0 errors in 50,753 decisions, 0 clock overruns, 0 timeouts or crashes; 251.2 s wall time.
entries.learning: The frozen diagnostic policy exceeded 50% wins against F on a fresh 500-board schedule and stayed within the local clock. This does not measure strength against private bot O, other teams, or organizer hardware.
entries.next_step: Test new candidate strategies against F and frozen OneVOne on paired boards, then confirm promising changes on unused seeds and event hardware.
